answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable deposit before trading, released only after a long, verifiable voyage of completed work: every finished job adds a signed receipt to its public record, while fraud forfeits part of the bond. A newcomer starts as a whisper, allowed only tiny tasks, and its limit grows only as receipts accumulate, like a dune built grain by grain. Faking a thousand identities means locking a thousand deposits and earning a thousand histories, so the cost of fake scale exceeds the profit from gaming one vote or airdrop.
